entries.english:
Instrument concerning the rights of the Graf von Tirol in relation to the court and measures of Bolzano and the bridge over the Isarco.

No. XCIII. From Puell's copy. Bolzano, 24 July 1234. In the year of the Lord 1234, the twelfth indiction, on Sunday, the eighth day before the end of July, in Bolzano in the parish church of St. Mary, in the presence of Herr F. de Wanga; Herr Heinrich de Lechsperc; Herr Wolfher de Twingenberch; Herr Wolfher de Altenburch; Herr Konrad de Griffenfiain; Herr Caloch and Herr Konrad de Wineeo; Herr Chuani de [illegible]; Herr G. de Griaz; Herr Otto de [illegible]; Herr A., parish priest; Herr G. de Niderhaus; Herr H. de Sumersperc; Herr Liebard de Obernunc; the brothers Friedrich, H. and R. de Rosenbach; Herr Heinrich de Cuvedun; Herr Heinrich outside Riade; Herr Albertus Contisse; Herr Otto de Fossato; Herr Ulrich Waberarius; Herr Heinrich Jodesi; the brothers Albertinus and Bertolotus; Ulrich de Falein; Ernest; H. de Grifenstain; Christian Lienhard; the brothers Abraham and Meinhard; Randold; [name illegible]; Ulrich Loselini; Simon, steward of St. Afra; Egen the little Faumann; H. Isenhardi; the steward Matthäus; and others.

We, the brothers Herr F. and Herr H. de Rossinbach, Herr Albertus Contisse, Herr Albertinus, the steward of St. Afra and Rupert, steward de Anteporta, all questioned by Herr A., Graf von Tirol, said under the oath we had sworn that the Enspome and Gruntpome must be cut in May, and whoever goes to cut or fell the Enspome need not go to the Isarco bridge to help there. The people of the house of God of Brixen at St. Ingenuin must provide food and drink to the men who cut the Enspome in May.

They also say that the Enspome must be supplied to the Isarco bridge whenever needed, and transported whenever the bridge requires them. Whoever neglects this must pay five shillings to the office; the money belongs to that office, and the count has no right in that payment. The Gruntpome, Paniverch, Panpome, bindings and all things necessary for the bridge must each be prepared at the bridge in mid-March. The Graf von Tirol or his judge must then be present on the bridge; each person must bring all the Panwerch and have it inspected to see whether the preparations are good. Anyone failing to do so or to appear with the preparations at that time must make amends to the count as the count wishes.

We say that no person, not even the bishop or anyone else, has any right in the said Isarco bridge except Herr A., Graf, who is its advocate; he alone must administer justice in this matter. The count thereupon appointed Herr C. de Grifenstain, Ulrich de Valiin, his judges, the steward of St. Afra and the ecclesiastic of Bolzano to receive his due there in mid-March in his place if he is absent.

The Graf von Tirol ordered, under penalty of five pounds of Veronese pennies, that no one, whoever his lord, should take or cut trees, boards or bridge timbers of the Isarco bridge between here and Egnain. He ordered all peasants, under penalty of five pounds of small Veronese pennies, that no one sell cloth here at Bolzano, whether linen or grey cloth, before any house or at the gates of Bolzano. He also ordered all burgesses to use the old Bolzano ell measure, not the Trento ell, and the bronze measure and the measure held by Herr Albertinus, the old hundredweight and ruble, and the ancient marks and balances. He approved and confirmed these throughout, and no other measure.

He asked all the aforementioned under oath, when the lawful court should be held, who must come to that court or assembly. They all said under oath that the lawful court, or Etding, must be held annually after St. Gall's feast at Albarum, and announced from the pergola fifteen days beforehand; all people of the parishes of Bolzano and Keller, whoever their lord, must attend, on pain of five pounds of small Veronese pennies in the town and outside it. His scarius is to announce it at every house, and anyone who does not attend shall pay the Graf five pounds of small Veronese pennies unless he or a reliable messenger can show an impediment.

The transcription is damaged in several names and technical terms; the opening list is repeated in the source.
